title: Honest run
summary: Every node follows the protocol. The verifiers' recomputed hidden states match the inferencers' within floating-point noise, and every segment is accepted.

title: Quantized model
summary: The node drawn to run segment 2 serves an 8-bit version of its layers while registered as full precision. Verifiers recompute that segment from its recorded inputs and the hidden states do not match.

title: Early termination
summary: The node running the last segment stops the answer early by reporting an end-of-sequence token that its own hidden state does not produce.

title: Forged output, caught
summary: A coalition holding a quarter of each group draws all four inference roles. It writes the answer with a much smaller model, then runs the real model once over that text so the hidden states look right. The last segment's verifiers decode the hidden states and find tokens the real model would not have chosen.

title: Forged output, accepted
summary: The same forgery, on a draw where the coalition also holds two of the three verifier seats on the last segment. The forged answer is accepted and the one honest verifier, who found the wrong tokens, is penalized. The paper's dispute step is open only to a rejected inferencer, so nothing in what we built reverses this.

title: Lazy verifier
summary: A verifier on segment 3 skips the recomputation, commits to states it did not compute and votes to accept, hoping to be paid for nothing.

title: Captured committee and dispute
summary: Two colluding verifiers are both drawn onto the three-member committee for segment 2 and vote down honest work with matching fabricated states. The inferencer disputes, and a larger second committee overturns the verdict.
